sense.text: A little heat from the beginning, so the wicked sisters don’t walk away from this class thinking they got a W this Sabbath. “All wickedness is but little to the wickedness of a woman: let the portion of a sinner fall upon her.” “So is a wife full of words to a quiet man.” If you are this type of wife, this class is not talking about you. You can listen to it, but it ain’t for you.

“A wicked woman abateth the courage, maketh an heavy countenance and a wounded heart: a woman that will not comfort her husband in distress maketh weak hands and feeble knees.” “Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.”

So the disclaimer stands from the start: if you are a wicked sister, not encouraging your husband, not taking care of your wifely duties, not taking care of the kids, not building up your house the right way, this is not about you. Sit back over in the cut, because some sisters will listen to this and look across at their husband like yeah, yeah, yeah, and they don’t clean, they don’t cook, and they disrespectful. This class is about the righteous sisters, the righteous wives, the ribs doing what they supposed to do, being a virtuous wife to their husbands.

The song This Woman’s Work is about a man whose wife is in a troubling, life-threatening childbirth where she may not make it. He is dealing with fear, helplessness, regret, the things he should have done with his wife and how he took her for granted. That is what the class is about.

Having kids is God’s plan. When the young get married, the first thing they want is to have kids, and the scripture speaks of it: “And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply.” That is what a husband and a wife do. Have kids. Have a lot of kids.

precepts.why:
“Lo, children are an heritage of the Lord: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.” The fruit of the womb is the man’s reward. “As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man; so are children of the youth. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them.” A man that has a lot of kids, he is happy.

In the world, having a lot of kids is looked at as a bad thing for our people: five kids in the house, no food to eat. Yet they put shows on with fourteen and fifteen kids and hype them up. In our community we get looked at bad for it, because they don’t want us to multiply. Exodus 1 shows it: the children of Israel multiplied. They understand that when there is more of us, we have more power, so they make having a lot of kids look like a negative thing when it comes to the Israelites, the Hispanics, the northern kingdom.

“Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house”: she brings forth a lot of kids. “Thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord.”

So it is a blessing. You fear the Lord, you are going to be blessed with a lot of kids.

“Children’s children are the crown of old men; and the glory of children are their fathers.” Children are a heritage, a crown to men, and the father is the glory of the children. The wife is to be a fruitful vine.

“He left behind him an avenger against his enemies.” When a man gets older and passes on, his mind is to leave behind an avenger: a child to finish fighting the war we are already fighting, to go out and wake up our people, to come against the other nations and teach our people who we are according to the scriptures.

We saw it in South Africa: young men teaching like young lions, young prophets bringing out the word. That is a crown to a man.

sense.text: Even though children are a blessing, we always have to consider that we are under the curses. “If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.” Those curses reach into the very bringing forth of our children.

precepts.why:
Among the curses we deal with in having children: “Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband.” In sorrow women bring forth children. Shout out to Eve, but that is one of the curses women go through.

It is said that having a child is the closest a woman ever gets to passing away, and under the curses, and by how the other nations deal with us, the mortality rate of Israelite women in childbirth is higher than any other nation’s. That is not to put fear in anybody for having a kid; it is the deeper meaning behind the song, a husband whose wife is going through it.

Throughout the scriptures, trouble and travail are compared to a woman giving birth. “For I have heard a voice as of a woman in travail, and the anguish as of her that bringeth forth her first child.” We know the labor pains, the contractions: the pain comes, eases up, and comes back stronger and stronger.

“The voice of the daughter of Zion, that bewaileth herself, that spreadeth her hands, saying, Woe is me now! for my soul is wearied because of murderers.” Woe is me now: when a woman is having a child, she is going through pain. That is one of the curses she goes through.

sense.text:
Whenever emotions come up we point at the sisters’ side of the room, but men in leadership know it is the brothers’ side that is very emotional. Brothers get corrected and don’t know how to deal with it: they leave, they stop talking, they sit in the back of the classroom, they get an attitude. There may be more murmuring on the men’s side of the room than on the women’s. Men are emotional too; the difference is we were never taught how to handle our emotions. The man in the song is dealing with guilt and regret and doesn’t know how to handle it.

“When I kept silence, my bones waxed old through my roaring all the day long.” That is what happens with a lot of men. When they are dealing with stuff, they keep silence. They come for counsel on how to study, how to break down scriptures, but not on what is going on inside their households and their personal lives. Those are the classes we don’t like, and those are the best classes, what we need to build ourselves up as a nation.

Like Denzel Washington in Fences, telling his son, who told you I got to love you: a man not knowing how to deal with his emotions, so he takes it out on everybody, his wife and his son. Antwone Fisher is another: a young man not knowing how to deal with his past.

“For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: my moisture is turned into the drought of summer.” This goes into holding sin in, but a lot of times we hold our emotions in the same way. And when you are faced with certain things, you start to think what if, why didn’t I, and the regret comes: regret over past behavior, over how you treated your wife. Hindsight is 20/20.

Neglect is part of it. Some brothers don’t take their wives anywhere but the bedroom, the kitchen and the school. We say Israelites have fun, the new moon, the Passover, and a lot of wives sit at home feeling like slaves. It ain’t supposed to be like that. A righteous wife carries a weight: bringing forth the kids and dealing with them, the leadership wives expected to fix the problems on the women’s side of the room, ordering the house, and dealing with you, your problems and the trauma you dump on her. Then you reflect and say, she deals with all this, and I don’t take her nowhere, I make her walk on eggshells. That is taking somebody for granted.

That is a good wife: “The grace of a wife delighteth her husband.” No matter what: he comes home and there are financial issues, he can’t find a job, the car broke, the insurance lapsed, everything happening in threes over and over. No matter what, she still delights her husband. That is the wives’ job: to make your husband happy.

“And her discretion will fatten his bones.”

“A silent and loving woman is a gift of the Lord.” A lot of times wives want to say something about this and that: you didn’t take the trash out, you didn’t hang the picture, you didn’t cut the grass. Every husband probably has five things he was supposed to do a month or a year ago, the honey-dos, the raised garden bed. A righteous wife knows that whining over and over is what the scriptures call a continual drip, so she sits back and won’t say anything about it, even if inside she is a little upset.

“And there is nothing so much worth as a mind well instructed”: her mind is well instructed in how a wife is supposed to be.

“A shamefaced and faithful woman is a double grace, and her continent mind cannot be valued.” Continent is self-restraint: able to go off about this, be mad about that, walk around the house over your clothes over here and this, that and the other, and she does not do it. She has self-restraint.

“As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.” If your wife goes out of town for a week or two, every cabinet door will be open, the cereal boxes on the counter, no clothes washed, and you smelling your shirt saying I can wear this again. You don’t realize what gets done, because it is automatic. Just as the women who think they are independent find out, once the man leaves, who used to do this and that, it is the same on the women’s side. Somebody has to stay up all night with the baby, and if the man has to go to work, it is going to be her.

So if you have a good wife ordering her house, doing the things, teaching the kids, some not working and homeschooling, some working and still homeschooling, that is her beauty.

“An harlot shall be accounted as spittle; but a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.” How is she a tower against death? Your wife knows you better than anybody on this planet. She knows the real you. We go out saying Shalom Israel, Christ bless, but she knows you are lazy, she knows you procrastinate, she knows you really don’t believe, that you don’t really watch classes. Some wives watch more classes and study more than their husbands.

And what does she do? Some go to leadership about their husbands, but the majority of good sisters sit back and hide all that. She holds it all in, and as men we 100% take that for granted, until you are faced with what the brother in the song is faced with.

Many wives feel like the woman in the James Baldwin clip: everybody else gets the best part of her husband and she gets the very minimum. Just fake it with me, she says; smile at me the way you smile at that boss. We go to work and smile, greet strangers, show everybody patience, respect and kindness, and then come home and dump all our anger and built-up aggression on our wives. They get the worst part of us.

“For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh.” Two become one. This builds into the relationship of Israel, the northern and southern kingdom coming together, and into how a husband is with his wife.

“This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church.” The relationship a husband should have with his wife is the same kind of relationship he should have with the church.

As leaders we counsel for an hour, two hours, even when Bishop says don’t counsel that long, tired and sleepy, trying to fix the husband and wife with an issue, the two brothers, the sisters. On the streets we see what our people are going through and we plead with them, teach them, sorrow with them. Then we come home and do the exact opposite. The way you are with your rib should be the same way you are with your church. If you are patient with the church, be patient with your rib. If you teach the church, teach your rib.

precepts.why:
“A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” A lot of us are one way on the outside, how the world sees us, and at home a completely different person. You can’t do that.

We think double-minded only means saying one thing and doing another, being a hypocrite, but this is double-minded too. You walk into the school and the kids are happy to see you, the brothers salute you, the sisters say Shalom, officer, Shalom, cap. And your wife is sitting over there because you just cussed her out for 45 minutes on the way to the school, wondering why everybody else is happy and she is not. We are double-minded and we trauma dump on our wives.

sense.text:
“Behold, thou hast instructed many.” A lot of brothers go out and teach many: we teach classes, some go to camp 30 days, 100 days, 365 days in a row. “And thou hast strengthened the weak hands.” A lot of people come into the body sick, needing help; a lot of marriages are messed up; and we dedicate our time to figuring out how to fix them.

As a leader in this truth, when people have your number your phone rings all day: can I counsel with you, I got a question. We answer the call, deal with the issue, and when we don’t know the answer we go to leadership to get counsel for their counsel. We make a lot of moves to fix other people’s lives.

“Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.” How many times have we told a brother, nah, let me go to the scripture, the Bible says this, put the cigarettes down, stop smoking weed? With people outside our household.

But inside our household, our wife asks a question and we sigh: there’s a class on that, go watch 15 Minutes with the Captains. Then she says what Bishop said, or what Captain Emmanuel said in his class, and we get mad. But you are not teaching her. We deal with everything on the outside and not on the inside of our households. The scriptures speak of our wife as a possession, and we don’t build up that possession.

“But now it is come upon thee”: all the things you dedicated your life to help, fix, change and build up, and now there is a kink in your own chain, something going on in your own household. “And thou faintest”: you don’t know what to do; I got a marital issue, my wife came to me, how do I fix this? “It toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.”

You spend months and years building up other people’s households, husbands and wives, teaching strangers on the street with ease, scriptures coming from everywhere. Now it comes on you and you freeze up and fold up. Most men don’t counsel about what is going on in their own household. The same thing you get on brothers to do, bring it up, don’t hold it in, when it comes upon us we go against our own counsel.

“Is not this thy fear, thy confidence, thy hope, and the uprightness of thy ways?” What is that fear? Men walk around saying I ain’t scared, I’ll die for this truth, I’ll die for you, brother. But that is not the fear we have. That fear goes into unresolved trauma, unresolved issues, things in our past we haven’t overcome. Faced with a challenge, we turn back into that little kid, that boyfriend that got cheated on, the issues we had with our ex-wives.

Trauma is not just what happened to you; it is what happened inside of you when what happened to you went unresolved. A father’s absence, a father’s neglect, a parent’s betrayal, a moment of abandonment. As men we don’t talk about not having our father in our life, or having a wicked mother or a wicked father, or a worldly father, which is almost like having an absent one because you weren’t learning the right thing. These are not just issues but blueprints, written into your code, imprinted on your mental DNA. That is why certain things your wife says take you back to when you were a child.

precepts.why:
“Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness.” A lot of us spend a lot of time restoring brothers. Brothers fall, sisters fall, people in the congregation fall, and we spend our time figuring out how to restore them, how to bring them back up into the position they were in and make them better than they used to be.

“Considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.” We do these things for others, the way Eliphaz says Job instructed many and upheld him that was falling.

sense.text:
What happens to men raised without a father in the household, raised by their mothers? Some women do the best job they can raising a man, but we know what the scripture says.

“As for my people, children are their oppressors.” Think of the YNs, the shysties, what they call the roadmen in the UK: breaking in your house and your car, pulling on door handles in the neighborhood. These are children oppressing the neighborhood, the grocery stores, and you.

“And women rule over them.” When young men are born in single-parent households, the women rule over them. “O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err.” They push the emotional side that women have onto the men: you stepped on my shoe, why you looking at me, and our young men end up killing one another. They fight their mothers’ battles. A son came into a store to defend his mother and got murdered. Ja Morant showed up with his goons at a shoe store to defend his mom, and his mom was wrong. That is the emotion men get from being raised by their moms in a single-parent household.

And without a father in the house, other men come in and out. So the son has an issue with his father for leaving and an issue with his mother for how he sees her carrying herself, which leaves him with a hatred for women and a hatred for men. The worst of both worlds.

precepts.why:
“There shall be a confusion also in many places, and the fire shall be oft sent out again, and the wild beasts shall change their places, and menstruous women shall bring forth monsters.” Watch the videos of kids going crazy, and their moms are in full agreement with it. Kids in a Florida project going crazy, the police show up, then the mom shows up and she is even worse, cussing everybody out, cussing the police out. She is training her kids to be just like that: little monsters.

So you need a man in the house. A child raised by just a father comes up almost as good as one with both parents. Having a father in your life is a great thing. Some women make the single-parent household work, but it is not the ideal situation.

sense.text:
No one taught us how to process emotion. Men are frowned upon for expressing how they feel; we are told to suppress, to be strong, not to break down. So sadness gets buried, fear gets converted into anger, and the mask is so convincing we forget what is underneath. We bottle it up, and we don’t take it out on our boss or the congregation or the brothers and sisters finding out who they are. We take it out on our spouse.

“Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.” The Bible tells us to confess our faults, and men don’t like doing that. Brothers will name you as their counsellor of a thousand when they haven’t talked to you in a year, because they don’t want to say they have no counsel. They’ll ask you to be their counsellor and never call, or call only to talk about what happened at camp, never about what they are dealing with.

To be relieved of that inner pain we must process it and channel it through God’s word. The problem is we don’t counsel about our issues, or we counsel with the wrong person.

precepts.why:
The wrong person is your wife. You go into all your emotional issues with her: when I was young this happened to me, this hurt me. You have to counsel about these issues, but there is somebody you shouldn’t be counselling with about them.

“Be not jealous over the wife of thy bosom.” This jealousy goes into resentment. You resent your wife because you unloaded all your emotional issues on her, and now y’all got mad and she throws them in your face: that’s why your mama used to beat you. Some sisters are evil and hit below the belt. Brothers for the most part won’t bust a window or key a woman’s car, but there is a whole song, I’ll bust the windows out your car, because when women get mad, the gloves are off. Everything you told her, they called you stupid in school, you couldn’t read, your stutter, comes back when y’all get into it, and you say I ain’t never telling nobody nothing.

“And teach her not an evil lesson against thyself.” Don’t teach her things about you that she can use against you.

“Trust ye not in a friend, put ye not confidence in a guide: keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.” Don’t be like Samson with Delilah, telling her all his secrets. Don’t counsel with your wife about stuff like that.

Who you need to counsel with is the brothers. Men need correction from other men. “Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.” As men we sharpen one another. Something going on, something from your past you are dealing with: go to a righteous counsellor, go to your brother, bring it to your brother.

“Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” The scripture says you should have one counsellor of a thousand, and that is true. But issues of the past sometimes should be brought up among a lot of men, because we find out we all have the same issues. Covert incest, mothers using their sons like boyfriends, not physical but mental: a lot of men have been through it and hold on to that trauma, thinking it is just them, until they talk and hear, yeah, that happened to me too.

Things that are real personal, keep to your one counsellor of a thousand. But you have to counsel about what you are going through. If you don’t, you bottle it all up and it explodes, and you push it out on your rib. That is why husbands end up hitting their wives: bottled up over and over, she pushes the button, you explode, and you do something you regret forever.

sense.text:
A narcissist helps strangers and treats his partner and kids the worst, because his emotional capacity is a cup with holes in it: it drains all day, and those closest get what is left. It is lacking empathy. Mad at every driver on the road, mad all day at work, and when you get home your wife gets it all. We push a stranger’s broken-down car into the parking lot in the heat, we get out of bed at 3 in the morning to give a brother a jump, and at home: why I got to take the trash out, I’mma hang the damn picture, stop badgering me. The holes can be plugged, but only by getting counsel and talking about the issues. Ignore it and the holes get bigger, until it reaches how you deal with your brothers and the congregation.

“This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves.” That is a narcissist: a man who loves his own self, who comes home thinking about nothing and nobody but himself.

“Unthankful”: some come home to a clean house and never say the house looks good, it smells like lavender and lemon in here.

“Without natural affection.” It should be natural to be affectionate toward your wife, to come home and want to hug her and kiss her. But we are mad from the whole day, our emotional capacity at zero, sometimes at minus ten: don’t bother me, leave me alone. Then the phone rings and a brother says come over, we going over the scriptures, let’s get a burger, and you are on your way. You just spent 30 minutes telling your wife to leave you alone, and that is where you want to be.

“Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof: from such turn away.” That form of godliness is the double-mindedness. You sit down, brothers surround you, you teach for one, two, three hours, go to Corinthians, go to Titus, go to Genesis, let me give you the breakdown, and your wife is dumb as a doornail when it comes to the scriptures. She doesn’t know the colour scriptures, no basic scriptures, nothing, because you don’t teach her, and when she asks a question you get mad.

You look clean on the outside, like the Pharisees, cleaning the outside of the cup; like whited sepulchres; hypocritical, as Romans 2 says. Meanwhile back at the ranch, ask her for a scripture that shows Jesus is black and she says Jesus wept, John 3:16. Your husband is a captain, an officer, y’all been in the truth 15, 20 years, and you don’t know no scriptures and can’t counsel a sister. Because he ain’t teaching her nothing.

precepts.why:
Your wife is supposed to be a representative of you; you are one body, you left your mother and father and the two became one flesh. “Hast thou a wife after thy mind?” Your wife is supposed to be after your mind. If you are good in the scriptures, good in history, a great counsellor, your wife should be a great counsellor.

“Forsake her not: but give not thyself over to a light woman.” You shouldn’t want a light woman, a wife not understanding the Bible, and that means you should be teaching your wife. She doesn’t have to break down the book of Daniel or 2 Esdras, but she should have a good basic understanding of the scriptures. If a sister calls and says I’m depressed, she should be able to deal with that, not come to you asking what do I tell her. You never taught her nothing.

Being a narcissist. “Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory.” A lot of households are run on strife and vainglory. “But in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.” You can’t run your household on ego.

Some don’t teach their wives because they don’t want her to know something they don’t know. They don’t want her to study, because one day she may ask a question he can’t answer, and his pride and ego take over. So he keeps her simple. There was a brother here, once a leader, whose wife couldn’t leave the house without him, couldn’t drive, didn’t know nothing.

You pour into everybody else but your wife. If she is supposed to be that tower against death, how will she do it if she can’t guide you with the scriptures? When your countenance is low, you don’t want her singing you a Maxwell song; you want her to go to the Bible and say remember what the scripture says, joy cometh in the morning. If you don’t build that tower up, it won’t be worth nothing. And then you come and counsel with us, saying my wife wicked as hell, she don’t know nothing. Were you studying with her? No.

sense.text:
Some of us men are narcissists, and some still live in the past. We get on the sisters about how they won’t forgive and won’t forget what happened in the world, and this side of the room is the exact same. We hold on to old arguments, old relationships, being cheated on. Instead of a bag lady you are a bag brother. You don’t trust her, not for something she did, but for what somebody else did to you. You get defensive and you compare.

The worst thing a woman can do is compare her husband to a man from her past or to her dad, my dad used to wash the cars and cut the grass. You don’t want to hear that: you should have married your dad, you should have stayed with that negro. But that works both ways. A woman doesn’t want to be compared to another woman either.

“There be three things that mine heart feareth; and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death.” Three things make the heart fail, but the fourth he was sore afraid of.

“But a grief of heart and sorrow is a woman that is jealous over another woman.” This is wisdom: those three are worse than death, and this fourth one is even worse than that. Think of Lorena Bobbitt, or Al Green and the hot grits. You don’t want a wife that is jealous over another woman, so let that stuff go: no more here we go again, you just like my mom, my ex used to do this. Women are different than men.

“And a scourge of the tongue which communicateth with all.” You are going to have a woman full of mouth. The scripture speaks of a silent and loving woman, and you won’t have one, because she won’t be silent and loving if she is jealous of another woman.

We read these scriptures with the women a lot, but hardly deal with the men on them. “Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before.”

Brothers, you have to follow the scripture too. You have to let the past go: the issues with your father not being around, how your father treated your mom, how your mom treated you, how your ex treated you, ex-girlfriends, ex-marriages. Let it go and move forward to what you have, or you will be in a worse situation. We have to look forward and figure out how to build this thing together.

precepts.why:
“Say not thou, What is the cause that the former days were better than these?” Never sit back and think, when I was with her everything was good, before you my life had no problems; my ex had the bathwater ready, the food always ready. Then you should have married her or stayed with her. But she didn’t believe in God and didn’t want to keep the commandments, so you left and found a woman who believes she is an Israelite, keeps the commandments and has the faith of Jesus Christ, and now you compare her to a wicked woman. You can’t build on that foundation. That’s wicked, and it makes a woman jealous over another woman.

“For thou dost not enquire wisely concerning this.” There is no wisdom in it. The children of Israel marched around the wilderness 40 years because they kept looking back: we were slaves in Egypt but the food was good. The manna tasted however they wanted it to taste, yet they weren’t happy; they wanted meat, God gave them so much quail they couldn’t take it, and they were mad again. Always looking back to their worst condition while the Most High was trying to free them.

So it is with the exes of the past: you were unequally yoked with a non-believer. Now you have a believer, so you have to build her up, teach her and raise her in the scriptures. If you keep going back to how things were, how will you encourage her to be godly? She’ll think, maybe if I go back to the club, smoke weed and get an OnlyFans, he’ll like me.

sense.text:
We treat strangers better than those we love, and speak to our spouse and children in ways we would never speak to a stranger, because we can get away with it. We compliment a brother on his haircut, a brother cuts his dreads off and it is a celebration in the school, but our wives sit eight hours in the beauty salon with their head under the dome getting microwaved, come home and ask can you tell I cut it, and we never say nothing. When was the last time you told your wife she does a good job?

But this is not a simp-out class. Don’t go home and start rubbing her feet all day and stop going to camp and stop travelling. “But this I say, brethren, the time is short: it remaineth, that both they that have wives be as though they had none.” We are in the last days. If you have a wife, you have to be as though you don’t; you have to do the Lord’s work and be about the Lord’s business. Brothers have a baby and the next week they are in Africa. The work has to be done, no matter what.

But when you are not doing the work, you have to make sure you take care of your responsibilities at home, your prized possession, your pillar of rest. Build that thing up, or she will be a pillar of stress.

“But he that is married careth for the things that are of the world, how he may please his wife.” You have to please your wife and take care of that responsibility. We have to teach this truth and travel the world, gone a month, two, three at a time, but at the same time take care of home. Why? Because she is teaching your kids. Do you want an unhappy, mean, angry, bitter, emotional woman bringing up your kids while you are gone? Your son will pick up those traits, and your daughter will too. Take care of that possession at home, or you will destroy it.

We deal with strangers better than we deal with anybody else. Some brothers sit there while an apologist runs up and talks trash, berates them and mocks them, and they just take it with the phone recording. On the street people are disrespectful and we take it; we find a way to restrain ourselves. Esau keeps walking and we turn our shoulder: you don’t shoulder bump that damn Edomite to the wall. But let your wife forget to do something, and at home you are ready for war, ready to cuss her out, tell her she ain’t ish. A sister comes up and you say get away from me, I got to sit in the room and play a game and doom scroll for two hours before I talk to you. Something ain’t right when you treat a stranger better than the person you exchange fluids with.

“And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works.” In the congregation we do that: we provoke brothers to love and good works, to keeping the commandments, and when they suffer loss we provoke them to love and good works. Then we go home and provoke our wives to nothing but being angry at us.

The index cards the sisters fill out tell it: my husband doesn’t want me to say good morning to him. One brother demanded his wife read so many chapters a day and bring him ten questions every day, with five or six kids she was homeschooling and him never there, when he couldn’t do that himself. We bring a militant mindset into the household out of fear and misplaced anger, thinking we have to rule our houses with our ego.

precepts.why:
“But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day.” We read it all the time, but how do you exhort your wife daily? Do you encourage her? Exhorting is encouraging one to do what is right. Some get their rest, say I’m out, are gone eight, nine, ten hours, come back, shower, change clothes and go to class, and say what’s up, and that’s it. That’s the relationship.

“Lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.” Exhort your wife daily too, not just the brothers in the body, because the scripture says she is the weaker vessel. On Telegram you get on the brothers, we got to communicate, we got to talk; in your household you say five words to your wife. If you have a dragon, you have to figure out how to slay the dragon. But if you have a wife who has your back, building up the house like the scripture says and taking care of your children, there is a disconnect.

If you don’t teach your wife, you are not teaching your daughter or your son either. You find an epiphany, something we had wrong forever, and don’t tell her, so she’ll read a verse and say that’s talking about this, rend your heart and not your garment, and embarrass you. Then you get mad when she says Bishop said, Captain said, Mother Shammar said. She references the only people she hears teaching the Bible. She should hear you teaching the Bible.

sense.text:
Familiarity is another reason we respect strangers: with strangers there are consequences, and you care how other people see you. At home you feel there is no consequence. Most good women don’t want to embarrass their husbands, so you know you can do what you want. Some have a good woman and treat her in reverse, like the brother singing love songs to a wife who just hit him in the face, only backwards.

“A son honoureth his father, and a servant his master: if then I be a father, where is mine honour?” A lot of times men only give honour where they think it matters. You honour your boss because it matters, you honour the men in the truth, you give double honour to the elders. But in your household: it don’t matter, she ain’t going to do nothing or say nothing, I can do whatever I want.

precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel.” You are supposed to give honour to your wife as the weaker vessel, and if something is weak, you have to build it up.

We are nicer to strangers than family out of impression management, assumed unconditional love, and accumulated history. Assumed unconditional love says: no matter what, you got to treat me right, you bound to me until I die, so I can treat you how I want and there ain’t nothing you can do. That ain’t right. That’s not scriptural.

sense.text: We have an emotional misplacement. “There is that speaketh like the piercings of a sword: but the tongue of the wise is health.” A lot of us get mad about something and go home and speak to our wives like the piercing of a sword.

precepts.why: “Be not as a lion in thy house, nor frantick among thy servants.” Don’t be a lion in your house, especially if you are a weakling in the streets. Out camping, you don’t want to call out sin: a homosexual walks by in high heels, hand on his hip, weave on, lace front and lipstick, halter top, veins coming out the bicep, and you afraid to go into the scriptures. You ain’t saying one word about the sin. Then you go in the house and become a lion.

“He winketh with his eyes, he speaketh with his feet.” Some of y’all go home and speak to your wives with your feet. “He teacheth with his fingers”: you put hands and feet on your wife. You are abusive to your wives, while out in the streets he says call me ma’am, and you roll up and say, next teacher.

sense.text:
A lot of problems in our households come because men try to keep score and throw it in her face: I provide, I pay all the bills, I do this, I take care of that. Congratulations for doing your job. Somebody says I take care of my kids: you supposed to take care of your kids, negro. I provide for my wife: you supposed to.

“But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” That is your job. You can’t throw in your wife’s face that you do what you are supposed to do. It is your reasonable service, a commandment of God. You can’t keep score in your house.

How do we fix this as men? “So ought men to love their wives as their own bodies. He that loveth his wife loveth himself. For no man ever yet hated his own flesh; but nourisheth and cherisheth it, even as the Lord the church.” You are supposed to love your wife like you love yourself. As said before, the relationship between Christ and the church is the same as between husband and wife: how you deal with the church should be how you deal with your wife and how you want to deal with yourself.

precepts.why:
You have to love your wife the correct way. You can’t love your wife while you speak with your feet and teach with your hands. “Husbands, love your wives, and be not bitter against them.”

Bitterness is nothing but unresolved issues with unmet expectations. Our expectations won’t be met until we get into the kingdom; until then we are labouring to enter into that rest. This ain’t our rest. There will be trouble in the flesh and problems, and it won’t be perfect yet. Don’t be bitter toward your wife.

You have to be able to control your spirit. You control your spirit at camp when a dude is standing in front of you with a six-pack and arms bigger than your thigh. “He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.”

So in the household you have to be slow to anger and deal with your wife as the weaker vessel. Now if you have a wife that is unruly and crazy, stand up for yourself; get your balls out of her pocketbook. But if you have a sister who does what she is supposed to do for the most part, it has to be a balance. Your wife can’t always see the worst part of you.

sense.text:
Sisters, how can y’all help? “Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence.” It is strange, insane, to hear of men that don’t want to have sex with their wives, of women complaining that their husbands don’t want them. It is a hard saying, like the disciples said when Christ taught that a man cannot put away his wife except for fornication: who can understand that, a man with his maid?

“And likewise also the wife unto the husband.” You render to your husband due benevolence. You want to fix a problem and ease his mind? Ease other things.

“Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” Respect and tone and how we deal with each other matter when we are addressing issues. So sisters, make sure you speak to your husband the right way. A soft answer turns away wrath.

precepts.why: “Every wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.” You can pluck it down with your hands by doing the things we talk about: complaining, yelling, arguing, being disrespectful, the neck dance. Your timing and how you approach certain things matters as a woman.

sense.text: This is about the man and the wife together. “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.” A man and a wife that agree together is beautiful before God.

precepts.why: How do they agree together? “Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God.” Y’all both agree that y’all are going to follow the Bible, follow the scriptures, follow the word of God.

sense.text:
Taking a counsel to a captain once, not knowing how to counsel it, the answer came back: Cap, you don’t have a daughter, so you are counselling from this side; you don’t want your daughter going through stuff like this. Those of us with daughters deal with it differently.

“Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.” So men, ask yourself: is the way you treat your wife the way you want your daughter’s husband to treat her? If the answer is no, you have to fix it. Fix yourself: deal with your past, drop the pride, don’t deal in misplaced anger, and don’t dominate with control.

“Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong. Let all your things be done with charity.” Quit you like men means conduct yourself like a man: keeping the commandments, with maturity, courage, discipline and responsibility. That is how you deal as a man, and that is how you deal with your wife in your household.

Brothers, we have to fix ourselves. Sisters, if you are a good wife, continue to be a good wife.
